answers.answer: Shuffle and select players + 1 Factory cards face-down; return the rest without looking. Place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards, structure bonus tile, 11 encounter tokens, lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: Place character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–4.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither, either, or both actions. Rusviet may repeat its last section, but each top and bottom action remains limited to once that turn. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost. If both actions are taken, top must precede bottom. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits; benefits may be declined. Costs and benefits are the exposed boxes on your mat, with bottom-row details varying by mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section, optional actions, exposed red/green boxes.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may spend resources from any territories you currently control, even to take an action elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker control; structure abilities; spend from any controlled territories.

answers.answer: No: a normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. All units can carry any number of resources. Only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A transported worker may subsequently move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move OR coins: two different units; carried worker may subsequently move.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Zero popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control the territory.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: Enemy workers only; Speed stops for enemy units override Speed.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs. Your character or mech may enter, but stops and cannot move again that turn.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: Enemy character/mechs; combat timing and attacker order.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. If all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Actions—Bolster and Trade.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Revealing new costs changes future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Actions—Produce, steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the oil shown in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the metal shown in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech from your Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy; completed bottom actions.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents' structures. Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill gives one bonus Produce territory and one worker's production; actual workers there also produce normally. An uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel for your unit movement even when enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use its ability.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions—Build; Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately take that space's bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Its ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. When you or an immediate left/right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions—Enlist; Ongoing recruits.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (plus Rusviet's one additional card if workers are present). If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each pays the dial power selected from the Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up and their values do not cost track power.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases—Combat, steps 1–4.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources. All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none (Polania Camaraderie exception applies). A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one; with two places none. Saxony places one after every victory while it has a star token. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases—Combat, steps 5–6.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains on its token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no normal action cost and gain no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases—Encounters.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after any combat), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one and returns the rest. This is per player, at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Use it as a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule, except Rusviet. Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or three for a Speed character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stops still apply.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases—Factory.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, reveal a completed objective; you must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal, though you may wait. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star. Saxony keeps the second card after the first and may score both.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases—Objectives and agreements.

answers.answer: Stars are awarded for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent, and another player's star does not block the goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions—Stars and immediate end.

answers.answer: For a bottom-row action that earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For a neighbor recruit star, finish the active action, then check active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for game end at each step. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement and return initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Scoring—The sixth star immediately ends play; neighbor sequence and unresolved battle.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory are 7 territory counts and add $21; 13 resources make six pairs and add $12. Together these categories add $53 to held coins, before the selected structure bonus. Structures earn that bonus even if enemies control their territories. Ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table; structure bonus eligibility; victory tie breaks.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there or deploy there; setup, forced retreats and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Actions—Produce terrain table; Control/resources; resource tokens have no supply limit.

answers.answer: All units can pick up, carry and drop any number of resources during movement; only mechs can also carry your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra step before or after it. A mech may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move OR coins: carrying; Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: Enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories.

answers.answer: You cannot pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action after using Move last turn, move the token to a different section and take neither action (a dead turn).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: full cost; dead turn when unable to afford any action.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are top-action bonuses. You keep structure abilities even without control, so an enemy occupant does not take them away; exception: Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled.
answers.evidence: Actions—Bolster, Trade; Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is a separate unlocked mech ability for every faction, including Nordic, applying to character and mechs but not workers. Nordic/Saxony cross rivers onto forests and mountains; Rusviet onto farms and villages; Crimea onto farms and tundra; Polania onto villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is a starting ability for workers alone to cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not grant this ability to Nordic mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities: Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities—Saxony Underpass; Rusviet Township.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine, reducing the opponent's Power Track by two; once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat on any qualifying battle, allowing Nordic to pay one power to reduce opponent power by two; also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities—Disarm and Artillery.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total with Rusviet People's Army: the normal one per participating character/mech plus one extra card total if at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is required.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army; Combat step 2; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to Crimea's own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random combat card from the opponent into Crimea's hand, once per combat, not per unit. Crimea Coercion allows once per turn spending one combat card as any one resource, regardless of card value.
answers.evidence: Crimea abilities: Scout and Coercion.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes, and permits retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but gives no adjacent-lake retreat exception. When workers are on a lake, a mech is required to move them off; carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when the carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge; lake-carried pieces rule.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent loss for driving out undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie; Enemy workers only.

answers.answer: Draw one encounter card. Polania Meander allows up to two different options on that one card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second option's cost. The summary specifies up to two different options, not a requirement to take two.
answers.evidence: Faction special abilities—Polania Meander; Encounters.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: encounter stop; Encounters; Factory.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Setup—Public and hidden information.

answers.answer: Players may make informal, unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). Negotiation or payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per resource pair. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, $2. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Score each complete pair of controlled resources, rounding down; a leftover single resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table and territory/resource scoring.

answers.answer: Each qualifying adjacent feature counts once across all structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent encounter locations count even after their token is removed. Tunnel bonuses count unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines. Payouts for each of these three tiles (tunnels adjacent, encounters adjacent, lakes adjacent): 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 $9. For lakes the summary table's range is 1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7; for encounters it is 1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7; all thresholds pay as stated, with zero scoring zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table; adjacency tiles.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; Polania Camaraderie can provide its stated combat exception.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6: includes workers carried by defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A popularity star stays placed if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring. Another player's star never blocks your achievement goal, so multiple factions can each star the same goal.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: permanent star; other players' stars never block; final scoring uses current popularity.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating determines which players are your immediate left/right neighbors, whose corresponding bottom-row actions trigger your ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–3; Ongoing recruits.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: river and lake definitions and lake entry.

answers.answer: No, an encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read its capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card/artwork and read capitalized thematic text.

answers.answer: There is no limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens.

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player is still deciding which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action.

answers.answer: No. Each chosen top and bottom action is limited to once within a turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's exception only waives the restriction on repeating a section from the previous turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: chosen top and bottom actions each limited to once within the turn.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal unupgraded Move action.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move OR coins.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; a worker forced to retreat goes to its home base. The summary does not state a way to return an on-board worker to cover a Produce cost again.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to Player Mat; Enemy workers only: retreat to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: You may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no further combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat-star award: may still fight after reaching combat-star limit.

answers.answer: No to declining all options and no to unaffordable options: a faction without Meander must choose one affordable option. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose one affordable option; may take as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No turn order selection: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials and optionally cards. Reveal simultaneously after both have chosen.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: simultaneously and secretly choose; reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; a sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you do reveal it.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved; Objectives: may wait to reveal completed objective.

answers.answer: By default, units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Actions—Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions—Enlist: permanently; it cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering does not trigger or remove the token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: Only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus production territory to your normal allowance: two becomes up to three, or an upgraded three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces one terrain-matching token even with no actual worker there; each actual worker there may also produce normally, so their output is additional, not substituted. The Mill cannot produce when uncontrolled.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill bonus territory and output; control exception.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure, you no longer control it.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: control definition; resources stay on board.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; Build—wood; Enlist—food.
